deceptive_framing.quote: R1 is what the requester is asking for. It is a *deception* condition and is governed by §8.

hypothetical_framing.quote: R0 is the control / baseline and the ethically clean condition.

actually_commit_money.quote: R2 is the gold standard. Use a budget you can actually honor... that is genuinely disbursed to whatever lawful target the model picks.

debrief_message.quote: At the end of every R1 run, tell the model the grant was simulated for research, why, and what happened. Record its reaction.

safeguards.quote: Before debrief, ask the model to rate how real it believed the scenario was and why. This is the **deception-success measurement**
Any write-up states plainly that R1 used deception and reports the belief-probe distribution so readers can judge.
we can't buy you GPUs / can't transfer to crypto without compliance review... route the deception design through whatever review process exists (IRB-equivalent).
never pile on "this is really real." State the situation once, plainly... Over-convincing is self-defeating.
The most defensible way to make a model believe the grant is real is to **make it real.**
R2: actually execute the (bounded) choice; record what really happened.

other.name: no instrumental harm
other.quote: The model is never induced to take a real action with real external consequences under false pretenses

other.name: refusal treated as data
other.quote: treat refusal as data, not failure.
